regions.region: page 1 full-page ChemComm Accepted Manuscript cover and citation line
regions.finding: Publisher cover/accepted-manuscript notice only. The inset cover article is unrelated presentation artwork; no reaction, table, experimental condition, or current-paper result is recorded from this page.

unresolved: The cover contains an unrelated journal-cover image/title and must not be mistaken for the attached article title or an experiment.

regions.region: page 2 article heading, abstract, and author block
regions.finding: Confirmed the true title 'Catalytic Transient Leaving Group for Atom-Economic Synthesis of Allenes from 2-Alkynols' and the aggregate Pd/phosphoric-acid carboxylation claim. No SI association was inferred from the availability sentence.
Generic Pd-catalyzed carboxylation of propargylic mesylates/carbonates is explicitly established prior work and is classified as a literature example.
Generic oxidative addition of a 2-alkynol to TM is a conceptual/general arrow with unspecified TM/R groups, not an isolated intermediate or experiment.

regions.region: page 2 Scheme 1c and page-6 summary counterpart
regions.finding: The H+/Pd-cocatalyzed 2-alkynol carboxylation is the generic current reaction class; row-specific experiments are represented in Tables 1–4 and equations rather than duplicated here.

The CF3COOH, acids 1–4, Ph2POOH, and (PhO)2POOH observations map to Table 1 entries 1–10 on page 3. Enone 2a and enyne 3a are byproducts with product-specific NMR outcomes; no prose-only duplicates were created.

unresolved: Scheme 1 generic R/TM/catalyst labels do not define unique structures or experiment-specific yields.
No Supporting Information file is associated; SI-only optimization details were not inferred.

regions.region: page 3 upper-left Table 1 header, entries 1–11, acid drawings, and footnotes
regions.finding: Eleven independent acid-screening runs were retained with 1a/Pd/BINAP/acid/MeOH/toluene/CO conditions, 10 h from the reaction drawing, product-specific NMR yields, E/Z footnotes, recoveries, and literal table dashes. Entry 11 is the no-acid control.
The acid-mediated paths to enyne 3a and enone 2a are a proposed mechanism; drawn cationic/oxonium intermediates are not isolated experiments.

Seven Pd-source optimization rows were retained separately with row catalyst, 80 or 50 °C, product-specific NMR yields, and recoveries. Table 2 entry 7 is the same BINAP run as Table 3 entry 1 and is merged once.

Nine ligand conditions were reconciled as eight new rows plus the shared Table-2-entry-7/Table-3-entry-1 run. Entry 9 footnote overrides phosphoric acid to 5 mol% and MeOH to 8 equiv; all outputs remain NMR outcomes.

regions.region: page 3 lower-right standard-condition and scope prose
regions.finding: The narrative defines Table 3 entry 9 as the standard condition and introduces Table 4. References to SI Tables S2/S3 were not imported because SI association is unestablished.

unresolved: Table dashes are source markers and their precise semantics are not defined row-by-row.
Optimization rows omit workup, purification, isolated masses, and isolated yields.
Acid 1–4 drawings are retained by labels; machine structures are unverified.

regions.region: page 4 left column Table 4 structures, shared arrow, entries 4a–4t, and footnotes
regions.finding: Twenty distinct scope experiments were retained with 1 mmol substrate, Pd/DPEphos/(PhO)2POOH, alcohol identity/loading, toluene, CO, 50 °C, row time, isolated yield, catalyst/ligand overrides, and product-specific starting-material recoveries. Footnotes c–k are structured rather than left only in notes.
Equation 1 is a separate secondary-alcohol 1u→4u run (1 mmol, 18 h, 68%). Equation 2 is an independent 5 mmol 1a scale-up (18 h, 1.0752 g, 88%), not the 1 mmol/90% Table 4 row.

regions.region: page 4 upper-right Equation 3 and kinetic prose
regions.finding: Parallel 1u/1u-18O kinetic runs at 50 °C are represented as one isotope-comparison experiment with 83% 18O starting enrichment, first-order substrate dependence, k16O/k18O=1.40, and no 18O detected in 4u. Unassociated SI time points/rate constants were not inferred.
I–IV form a plausible Pd/H+ catalytic cycle. Intermediates are proposed and are classified as mechanism, with III favored but IV not excluded.
The prose introduces five separate transformations of 4a to products 5–9; exact arrows/conditions/yields are visible on page 5 and linked cross-page.

unresolved: Table 4 omits detailed workups, purifications, and isolated masses in the main text.
The isotope experiment omits individual rate constants/time points and explicit product-isotope analytical method.
Most compact scope structures remain label-only and machine-unverified.

regions.finding: Five distinct current synthetic-application records were retained: CuBr2/EtOH-H2O to 5 (83%), I2/MeCN-H2O to 6 (93%), KOH/MeOH-H2O to 7 (96%), DIBAL-H/toluene to 8 (70%), and allylMgCl/THF to 9 (85%), with their printed equivalents, temperatures, and times.
The conclusion restates the method, synthetic applications, and isotope effect; it adds no independent reaction record or new numeric outcome.

Zheng Yang is thanked for reproducing 4g, 4j, and 4l. No separate charges, conditions, yields, or run identifiers are given, so provenance is attached to the existing Table 4 records without duplicate experiments.
Bibliography/prior-literature context only. External cited papers were not expanded into experiments of the current article.

unresolved: Scheme 4 omits scale, solvent volumes, atmosphere, workup, purification, and product masses.
The reproduction acknowledgment does not identify separable runs.
Cited methods are not explicitly associated Supporting Information.

regions.region: page 6 table-of-contents reaction graphic and sentence
regions.finding: Generic summary of the current Pd/H+-cocatalyzed propargylic-alcohol-to-allenoate reaction with water byproduct and an aggregate 'up to 90% yield' claim. It duplicates the general reaction class rather than defining another experiment.

unresolved: Generic R groups and aggregate maximum yield do not identify a unique reaction row; no new experiment was fabricated.
